Boundary: cartesian_vector_components_3d (signed parent) supplies components, cited not re-derived; moment_of_force_scalar_2d (signed) is the 2D analogue whose single scalar term M_O = x Fy - y Fx is the planar special case, and this skill is its 3D vector extension; position_vector_3d (batch sibling) owns FORMING r from two points - r is taken here as a given Cartesian vector and is never constructed from coordinates; dot_product_projection (batch sibling) owns the dot product as a PROJECTION tool - this skill uses a dot product ONLY as a perpendicularity verification and states that narrow use in concept, procedure and solution, computing no projection; moment_about_specified_axis, moment_of_force_vector_3d, couples and force-couple reductions are excluded as downstream or separate. Worked example Operator-re-derived from the on-disk prompt and cross-checked against both the component form and the cofactor form: r = 2i - 3j + 4k, F = 1i + 5j - 2k; i-component (-3)(-2) - (4)(5) = 6 - 20 = -14; j-component -[(2)(-2) - (4)(1)] = -(-8) = +8; k-component (2)(5) - (-3)(1) = 10 + 3 = 13; M_O = -14i + 8j + 13k. Distinguishing feature bites: all three moment components are nonzero and distinct in magnitude, so the result does not lie along a single axis and cannot be obtained by the signed 2D scalar method; dropping the alternating j-minus yields -14i - 8j + 13k and reversing the operands yields 14i - 8j - 13k, both distinct from the correct result and from each other, so each mapped signal routes to its own answer; negatives are present in both inputs. F = -14 + 40 - 26 = 0, both closing exactly. THREE-signal mapping: axis_confusion at step 3 (the cofactor cross-term pairing - which r-component pairs with which F-component for each output axis), sign_or_placement_error at step 4 (correct pairings but a dropped or flipped alternating j-minus, or F x r written in place of r x F so the sense reverses; a distinct authored act from step 3, not a duplicated crux), unclassified at step 7 (report and boundary - incomplete Cartesian moment, magnitude-only headline, skipped verification, projection drift, r constructed from coordinates, or reaching into axis reduction or couples). solution_sequencing_error OMITTED: the three cofactors are computed independently and no authored step strands a prerequisite on an out-of-order solve. simple_average_used omitted (Centroids-family).
